title: International politics
subtitle: negotiation, minorities, solidarity, delegate
summary: Talk about international organisations, political movements and conferences - pursuing aims, upholding rights, negotiating, and handling delicate issues with unity.

lesson.heading: The United Nations
lesson.text: The UN is an international organisation **constituted** - formed - in 1945 to make the world a better place for **humanity**, all people. From its **foundation**, when it was established, it has **pursued** key aims: to keep peace, to **establish** friendly relations between countries, and to work together to **conquer** poverty, disease and **illiteracy**.

examples.text: From its **foundation** it has **pursued** these key aims.
The government wants to **establish** a committee to work on reducing poverty.
The organisation's aim is to **conquer** illiteracy throughout the continent.

lesson.note: Pursue collocates with aim, goal, career and strategy: Lesley is determined to pursue her goal of becoming a barrister.

lesson.heading: Negotiation, justice and intervention
lesson.text: The UN stresses the importance of **negotiation**, discussions in an attempt to reach an agreement. It is opposed to **injustice** - unfairness - and **upholds** (supports) the rights of **minorities**. It will only support military **intervention** if the Security Council agrees that this is **justified**, that is, that there is a good reason for it.

examples.text: It is hoped that the current **negotiations** will lead to a positive outcome.
There is still too much **injustice** in the world today.
The rights of ethnic **minorities** are sometimes neglected by national governments.
It is impossible to **justify** the use of force in such a situation.

lesson.note: Minority collocates with adjectives like ethnic, religious and oppressed.

lesson.heading: Political movements
lesson.text: A **political movement** is a group of people with the same beliefs working together to achieve something. They often use a **slogan**, a short phrase that catches attention and is easy to remember. The aim might be the **liberation** of a minority, or the **integration** of a social group into the society from which it feels excluded.

examples.text: Left-wing political **movements** were particularly powerful in the early 20th century.
On the whole this society is very well **integrated**.
The aim of the movement was the **liberation** of an oppressed minority.

lesson.heading: Marches and solidarity
lesson.text: Members of a political movement sometimes go on a **march**, a walk where they demonstrate their **solidarity** with others who share the same attitudes and aims.

examples.text: Are you planning to go on the protest **march** tomorrow?
The workers expressed their **solidarity** by organising a huge demonstration.

lesson.heading: International conferences
lesson.text: **Delegates** - representatives - from 60 countries are attending. Their aim is to minimise the energy requirements of each country's **infrastructure**, its basic systems and services such as transport. Governments **recognise** (accept) the importance of the discussions and have **undertaken**, that is promised, to support the measures agreed.

examples.text: Chris is going to the conference as our **delegate**.
The country's economy can only develop once it has a good **infrastructure**.
The party **undertook** not to reduce spending on international aid.

lesson.heading: Delicate issues and unity
lesson.text: Some of the issues under discussion are **undeniably** - certainly - **delicate**, that is they need to be handled with great skill. Even so, the conference has shown more **unity**, more being together as one, than is **customary** (usual) at such gatherings.

examples.text: It is **undeniably** true that the project is likely to meet with some opposition.
It's quite a **delicate** subject, so take care how you bring it up.
Is it **customary** in your country to take a gift if you visit someone's house?

exercises.prompt: Match each verb with its noun.
The organisation's aim is to ___ illiteracy throughout the continent.
exercises.explanation: To conquer a problem is to beat it or get rid of it.

exercises.prompt: There is still too much ___ in the world today.
exercises.explanation: Injustice is unfairness; the adjective root is just.

exercises.prompt: The rights of ethnic ___ are sometimes neglected by national governments.
exercises.explanation: Minorities are groups who differ racially or in some other way from most people where they live.

exercises.prompt: The government wants to ___ a committee to work on reducing poverty.
exercises.explanation: To establish something is to set it up or put it in place.

exercises.prompt: Lesley is determined to ___ her goal of becoming a barrister.
exercises.explanation: Pursue collocates with aim, goal, career and strategy.

exercises.prompt: It is ___ true that the project is likely to meet with some opposition.
exercises.explanation: Undeniably means certainly - it cannot be denied.

exercises.prompt: The workers expressed their ___ by organising a huge demonstration.
exercises.explanation: Solidarity is the feeling of unity with others who share the same attitudes and aims.

exercises.prompt: Is it ___ in your country to take a gift if you visit someone's house?
It's quite a ___ subject, so take care how you bring it up.
exercises.explanation: A delicate issue needs to be handled with great skill.

exercises.prompt: The country's economy can only develop once it has a good ___.
exercises.explanation: Infrastructure is the basic systems and services of a country, such as transport.

exercises.prompt: The party ___ not to reduce spending on international aid.
exercises.explanation: To undertake to do something is to promise to do it.

exercises.statement: A slogan is a short phrase that catches people's attention and is easy to remember.
exercises.explanation: Correct - political movements often make use of a slogan.

exercises.statement: Military intervention means staying out of a difficult situation in another country.
exercises.explanation: Intervention is involvement in a difficult situation in order to improve it.

exercises.explanation: Negotiation is discussion in an attempt to reach an agreement.
